audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest may break the equity-OE debt treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: capitalized interest unquantified; computed annualized interest is $6.17 million on $133.5 million at 4.62% and $11.64 million on $253.0 million at 4.6%, equal to 3.2%-6.1% of the $192.2 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized financing cost bypasses the equity-level OE numerator while debt principal is intentionally not deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The weighted average interest rate on the revolving credit facility was 4.62 % as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: Trex had funded borrowings but reported no 2025 net interest expense or cash interest net of capitalized interest. The exact capitalized amount and sustainable debt balance remain unresolved. The June 2026 snapshot implies a recurring cost large enough relative to anchor OE to change the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2025-2026 capitalized-interest rollforward and average debt balances, determine the post-commissioning financing burden, and rerun every scenario with the after-tax recurring interest cost not otherwise captured in OE.

audit_findings.title: The reduced share denominator may not bear the financing cost used to obtain it
audit_findings.magnitude: $153.557 million of H1 2026 repurchase cash, $119.5 million increase in debt, and 3.872 million reduction in outstanding shares; using 102.145 million rather than FY2025 diluted shares of 107.096 million mechanically raises base value from approximately $25.28 to $26.50 per share, or $1.22 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The current share denominator captures post-anchor repurchases, but FY2025 OE does not capture the associated 2026 financing cost or cash use.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of shares of the registrant’s common stock outstanding on February 5, 2026 was 105,737,365 .
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, while the precise funding attribution remains unresolved. Repurchases and substantially higher debt occurred together, and H1 2026 already reports $2.327 million of net interest expense. The denominator effect alone is about 4.8%, before accounting for normalized interest, making the issue material to per-share value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each 2026 repurchase to operating cash, cash balances, and incremental borrowing; calculate the current fully diluted denominator; then rerun using that denominator with the corresponding normalized after-tax interest burden and any required bridge treatment.

audit_findings.title: Long-duration warranty claims could exceed the expense embedded in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $29.740 million recorded reserve versus a filed $24.8-$45.6 million possible-loss range; $15.860 million to the top of that range, while exposure above the range is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated recurring warranty provision would overstate OE; an unrecorded obligation for prior sales could also reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Actual experience could exceed the range due to uncertainty associated with the future number of claims expected to be closed with some payment and estimates of the costs associated with servicing those claims.
audit_findings.explanation: Reserve-estimation uncertainty is demonstrated, but an actual deficiency is not. The top of the filed range exceeds the booked reserve by $15.86 million, only about 0.6% of base equity value if treated solely as an incremental liability. Claims beyond the range or a persistently inadequate recurring provision could be larger, but the supplied record cannot establish that magnitude.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the actuarial best estimate, claim-frequency and severity sensitivities, and subsequent claims triangles; rerun any demonstrated recurring provision shortfall through OE and any prior-period shortfall through the bridge without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The ten-year OE history may mix LIFO and FIFO accounting bases
audit_findings.magnitude: 2024 net income increased $12.054 million and 2023 net income decreased $1.265 million under FIFO; computed cumulative adjustment at January 1, 2023 was $26.193 million, versus a $47.8 million gap between the $240 million trend and $192.2 million binding anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Inconsistent inventory accounting can distort historical OE volatility and growth analysis, but it does not directly change the latest-actual anchor or bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fourth quarter, the Company changed its accounting method of valuing inventory from a last-in, first-out (LIFO) method to a first-in, first-out (FIFO) method.
audit_findings.explanation: The historical comparability problem is demonstrated if 2016-2022 came from unrecast filings. It is not material to the supplied valuation because the latest-actual $192.2 million anchor binds below the $240 million trend, and the scenarios use conservative business-default growth rates. The largest filed annual adjustment, $12.054 million, is also far below the $135.5 million 2021-2022 OE reversal supporting the too-hard designation.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2016-2022 OE on FIFO for the audit trail and rerun only if the consistent-basis trend falls below $192.2 million or changes the selected growth regime.

audit_findings.title: A flat bear case may not capture concentrated-customer downside
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $857.2 million of FY2025 sales across three customers, computed as 73% of $1.174267 billion; single-customer downside unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A customer loss or destocking cycle would reduce future sales, margins, OE, and potentially terminal growth below the modeled bear path.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, three customers represented approximately 73%, 81%, and 72%, respectively, of the Company’s total net sales.
audit_findings.explanation: The 73% concentration is demonstrated, but no actual customer loss or sustained destocking is shown. This is therefore a forward-looking scenario risk rather than a present error in OE. Its materiality depends on individual customer shares, replacement volume, and associated contribution margins, none of which are supplied.
audit_findings.action: Obtain customer-level sales and contribution margins and stress a multi-year loss or destocking by the largest customer, including operating-deleverage and terminal-growth effects.

audit_findings.title: The anchor retains identifiable Arkansas start-up inefficiencies
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.5 million of filed 2025 SG&A start-up cost, approximately $1.845 million after tax at 26.2% and 1.0% of anchor OE; gross-margin start-up inefficiencies are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary start-up costs depress the FY2025 OE anchor and, if projected as permanent, depress every scenario's operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease was primarily the result of higher raw material costs on aluminum and steel, tariffs, changes to production process driven by refinements made to our Enhance ® decking product line, and inefficiencies associated with start-up costs at our Arkansas facility, partially offset by higher pricing.
audit_findings.explanation: The identified $2.5 million SG&A component is demonstrably embedded in the anchor but is small on its own. Additional Arkansas inefficiencies were included in cost of sales without a disclosed amount, and ramp costs may continue until or after decking production begins in 2027. The record therefore cannot establish the total normalization or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a facility-level schedule separating the $2.5 million SG&A cost and cost-of-sales inefficiencies from recurring operating expenses, verify the commissioning timetable, and rerun with only demonstrably temporary costs phased out as they cease.
